Definition: from G846 and G3700; self-seeing, i.e. an eye-witness:--eye-witness.
BiblicalUsage: Luke opens his Gospel by saying it came from those who were eyewitnesses from the very beginning. The word means someone who saw it with their own eyes, not someone who heard it second-hand.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the Christian faith rests on what people actually saw, and Luke knew that mattered enough to say so in his first breath.
